messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Dedicated pool saturation detected for tenant=acme-enterprise (pool=dedicated-us-west-2-acme)
incident-bot: severity=sev2, metric=GPU_UTIL, value=99.8%%, pending_pods=12, queued_requests=183
incident-bot: runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/dedicated-pool-saturation

alice_oncall: ack. I'm on it. Paging eng-runtime and infra.

bob_sre: seeing the same in metrics. All 8 GPUs on that pool are at 98-100%%. Autoscaler not triggering — scale policy is max_replicas=8, burst not enabled for this tenant.

alice_oncall: timeline: this started ~2m ago after a large batch job from Acme. Their app sent a traffic spike ~4k concurrent requests.

clara_runtime: tagging in. Do we have KV cache/inference-cache hits? If cache hit rate crashed we might be overloaded by repeated context windows.

alice_oncall: cache hit-rate dropped from 72%% to 14%% for that tenant in the last 5m.

clara_runtime: that explains token amplification. Also note many requests are using long seq lenses (>=1024). Bigger memory pressure.

bob_sre: quick checks:
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-acme -> many pods in Pending (InsufficientGPU)
- gpus available in cluster: 0
- autoscaler events: max_replicas hit

jen_ops: I can provision a small burst pool (2x A10s) in the account's dedicated namespace if we approve. Provision time ~6-8m.

alice_oncall: options: (A) enable burst capacity for acme -> give them 4 extra GPUs (fast), (B) force-evict low-priority background pods in pool, (C) throttle tenant traffic via gateway rules, (D) migrate heavy requests to a quantized model variant on hosted fallback.

dan_acct: Acme is on an annual reserved plan but we promised predictable throughput. They are on a support call now. Need ETA and mitigation plan.

matt_eng: quantized variant (gpt-small-q4) exists and we've validated answer parity for most workloads. Could route heavy batch jobs there temporarily.

alice_oncall: immediate mitigations I propose:
1) Enable burst (jen) + add 4 GPUs to pool (temp).
2) Apply a per-tenant soft rate-limit of 60rps for non-interactive routes.
3) Route long-seq batch requests to quantized fallback model for 10m.
4) Start account notification and postmortem ticket INC-1980012345.

jen_ops: provisioning now (requested via infra CLI):
```
infra provision-burst --tenant acme-enterprise --gpus 4 --region us-west-2 --ttl 1h
```
jen_ops: provisioning accepted, job id=burst-789. Estimated ready: 7m.

bob_sre: applying gateway throttle rule (nonblocking) now.

bob_sre: ```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking/v1
kind: TrafficPolicy
metadata:
  name: acme-soft-throttle
  namespace: gateway
spec:
  match:
    tenant: acme-enterprise
  rateLimit:
    requestsPerSecond: 60
    burst: 30
EOF
```

clara_runtime: starting canary reroute of model calls matching "batch/*" to gpt-small-q4. Script run:
```
redwood route update --tenant acme-enterprise --selector batch=true --model gpt-small-q4 --canary 100
```
clara_runtime: canary complete (100%%) for those routes, latency improved, quality spot-check ok for 20 samples.

alice_oncall: status update: burst provisioning in progress, throttle applied, canary in place. Pending: provision finish, pending pods draining/starting.

incident-bot: update: burst-789 state=provisioning -> running (6m)

jen_ops: new nodes joined the pool. Kube reports 4 new GPU resources.

bob_sre: autoscaler now sees capacity. K8s scheduled 6 previously Pending pods; 6 still Pending due to image-pull delays.

matt_eng: image pull throughput is slow for large model images; initiating parallel pulls on nodes.

jen_ops: forced image pre-pull on new nodes to speed start.

bob_sre: all pending pods transitioned to Running. GPU utilization dropped to 78%%. Queued requests down to 12.

alice_oncall: Acme on call says throughput is returning; they saw ~4-5 minute degradation window. They want root cause and whether long-term changes required.

dan_acct: relaying to Acme: thanks for the quick work — they want a postmortem and confirmation on SLAs.

clara_runtime: next steps (post-incident):
- Increase max_replicas for that pool to 12 and enable tenant burst policy with cap 6 for future bursts.
- Add a model-card recommendation to customers using long sequences to use prefix-caching.
- Improve image-pull strategy (smaller model layers, registry nearer to region).
- Add alert rule: if pending_pods > 5 and cache_hit_rate < 25%% -> auto-throttle non-interactive routes.

alice_oncall: agreed. I'll create ticket INC-1980012345-POSTMORTEM and assign to eng-runtime + eng-infra. Drafting customer summary now.

bob_sre: handoff to night oncall (mike) in 30m. I will summarize in pager and pin runbook link.

alice_oncall: thanks team. Closing real-time mitigation. Leaving canary and throttle in place for 20m for safety, then we revert as part of cleanup.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to sev3. Customer impact: 5-8 minutes of elevated latency/errors for acme-enterprise. Mitigations applied: burst provisioned, soft throttle, model fallback. Ticket: INC-1980012345

matt_eng: note for postmortem: customer had a scheduled internal batch at 10:02 PDT that correlated with spike — suggest we add rate-limit guardrails to reserved pools for scheduled large jobs.

alice_oncall: Acknowledge. I'll include that in the postmortem action items. handing off to bob_sre for overnight watch.

bob_sre: I have it. marking thread resolved in 10m unless new alerts. :thumbsup:

jen_ops: cleanup script to revoke burst after 1h scheduled. I'll also prepare a shorter TTL option for future bursts.

alice_oncall: final note to include for customer email: timeline, root cause hypothesis (cache drop + max_replicas cap), actions taken, immediate remediation, and follow-ups (increase max_replicas, enable burst, registry improvements).
